title: Graduate Premium Evidence and Content Assets
problemSolved: The value of a King's education is too easy to assert in general terms and too hard to evidence in specific, audience-relevant ways.
whatChanges: King's develops evidence packs that combine outcomes, destinations, stories, employer insight and distinctive King's experiences.

decisionLog.outcome: Reconstructed 2.4.1 around a tighter boundary: the deliverable creates evidence-backed graduate premium fact packs, narratives, messaging frameworks and rich media assets for faculties, departments and disciplinary areas. It does not own mobilisation, channel strategy, campaigns or audience activation, which sit in 2.4.4 and other consuming activity. The working mobilisation model is three annual stages: prove the model and creative standard in Year 1, broaden the asset base in Year 2, and build critical mass and a renewable evidence estate in Year 3. Indicative incremental investment is £30,000 in 2026/27, £60,000 in 2027/28 and £100,000 in 2028/29, with editorial direction provided through faculty and central marketing expertise and analytical/project capacity drawn from shared King's Edge resources.

Clarified the early Year 1 rich-media commitment as six proof-of-concept video exemplars at faculty, department or disciplinary level. The exemplars should show how the distinctive features of a King's education translate into employability advantage, using graduate outcomes and destinations, disciplinary strengths, student and alumni stories, employer insight and distinctive King's experiences to build substantiated Graduate Premium claims and establish a reusable creative and evidence standard.
decisionLog.notes: Any pre-business-case media funding is an early release against the existing Year 1 rich-media and production envelopes, not additional programme cost. 2.4.1 owns production of evidence-backed media assets; campaign strategy, targeting and paid activation remain with 2.4.4.
